'''Dahlia Greidinger''' ({{Langx|he|דליה גרידינגר}}; nee '''Katzenelbogen-Katz''', July 27, 1926 – July 16, 1979) was an Israeli scientist who helped develop the country's chemical industry.

==Early life, family and education==
Dahlia Greidinger was born in [[Neve Tzedek]], [[Tel Aviv]]. She was a fifth generation [[Sabra (person)|Sabra]]. Her parents were Miriam Rokach and Joseph Katzenelbogen-Katz.

She attended the [[Hebrew Reali School]] of [[Haifa]]. She earned an M.Sc. in chemistry from the [[University of Lausanne]], Switzerland, where she graduated with distinction.<ref name="technion bio">{{cite web |title=Dr. Dahlia Gredinger |url= http://tx.technion.ac.il/~aggreid/Dalia.html| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20050909024850/http://tx.technion.ac.il/~aggreid/Dalia.html |website= technion.ac.il | publisher= [[Technion — Israel Institute of Technology]]| archivedate= September 9, 2005| url-status= |access-date= 25 August 2020}}</ref>

==Career==
Returning to Israel after her education in Switzerland, she was the first editor of ''Israel Scientific Council Magazine''.<ref name="technion bio" /> In 1951, Greidinger became a teaching and research assistant at the [[Technion — Israel Institute of Technology]].<ref name="technion bio" /> After completing her doctorate in 1958, she began working  at Deshanim Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd. By 1969, she was appointed director of Research and Development and elected to the board of directors.<ref>{{cite web | url= http://b7prt05.iclfertilizers.com/irj/servlet/prt/portal/prtroot/com.sap.portal.navigation.portallauncher.anonymous?NavigationTarget=ROLES://portal_content/com.sapro.iclportal/roles/com.sapro.portal_user/Production_Marketing/com.sapro.Fertilizers_And_Chemicals/com.sapro.F_CH_About_Us| website= iclfertilizers.com| title= Fertilizers & Chemicals}} {{Dead link|date=July 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The company grew to become Israel's largest supplier of  fertilizers.

Greidinger wrote for scientific publications and was the holder of several patents, among them a patent on Controlled release particulate fertilizer composition,<ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.freepatentsonline.com/4378238.html |title= Controlled release particulate fertilizer composition| date= | website= freepatentsonline.com| access-date= }}</ref> 'Stable liquid N-P-K fertilizer composition and method of use',<ref name= "United States Patent 4318729">{{cite web| url= http://www.freepatentsonline.com/4318729.html |title= Stable liquid N-P-K fertilizer composition and method of use| date= | website= freepatentsonline.com| access-date= }}</ref> a liquid fertilizer composition storable for 6–8 months, and Solid Ammonium Polyphosphate Compositions and Manufacture.<ref name="Canadian Patent 1104790">{{cite web| url= https://brevets-patents.ic.gc.ca/opic-cipo/cpd/eng/patent/1104790/summary.html| title= Solid Ammonium Polyphosphate Compositions and Method for the Manufacture thereof| website= patents.ic.gc.ca| publisher= Canadian Intellectual Property Office | date= | access-date= February 24, 2021}}</ref> She was a member of the European Committee for Expansion, the Association of Academic Women and the Anti-Cancer Association.<ref name="technion bio" />

==Legacy==
The Feinberg Graduate School of [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] awards a fellowship for cancer research financed by the Dahlia Greidinger Anti-Cancer Fund.<ref name="Jewish Virtual Library">{{cite web |title=Israeli Women in Science & Technology |url= https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/israeli-women-in-science-and-technology |website=Jewish Virtual Library |access-date=25 August 2020}}</ref> In honor of her contributions in the field of chemistry and fertilization systems, the family established the Dahlia Greidinger Fertilizer Research Fund.

==Personal life==
She married Kalman (Coleman)<ref name= expansion>{{cite news| title= Cineworld: Behind the Scene: From early talkies to talking turkey on global expansion| url= https://www.thetimes.com/world/us-world/article/cineworld-from-early-talkies-to-talking-turkey-on-global-expansion-8xzp6nt6q| first= Alexandra |last= Frean| date= December 6, 2017| work= [[The Times]]| url-access= subscription| access-date= February 24, 2021}}</ref> Greidinger, a cinema company businessman,<ref name= then>{{Cite news|url=https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-first-haifa-then-tel-aviv-then-the-world-1001313569|title=First Haifa, then Tel Aviv, then the world| first1= Zeela |last1= Kotler Hadari | first2= Assaf |last2= Uni| date=5 January 2020|work=[[Globes (newspaper)|Globes]] |language=en}}</ref> in October 1950. They had four children,<ref name="technion bio" /> including sons [[Mooky Greidinger|Moshe ("Mooky")]] and Israel, who were leaders in their father and grandfather's successor company, [[Cineworld]] until 31 July 2023, when it was announced that Mooky and his brother will leave Cineworld, after the company entered Chapter 11 process in September 2022.<ref name= then /><ref name= expansion />

She died of cancer in 1979, after ten years with the disease.<ref name="technion bio" />
